technical.summary: Bullish structure with price above all key MAs and positive momentum indicators, but weak trend strength (ADX 10.87) and overbought conditions (Stoch 84.5, StochRSI OB) create limited upside potential and elevated pullback risk.

fundamental.summary: SNPS shows no insider buying conviction, no institutional accumulation signal, zero government contracts, no lobbying activity, minimal retail interest, and elevated earnings risk within 28 days—insufficient smart money alignment for actionable signal.

sentiment.summary: No congressional signal; fear sentiment (37/100) presents contrarian opportunity, but lack of insider buying conviction and absent news data limit bullish conviction.

risk.summary: Severe macro headwinds: VIX at crisis levels (345), flat yield curve signalling recession risk, rising dollar pressuring multinationals, with earnings event in 28 days adding execution risk.

debate.key_bull_argument: Price above all major moving averages with positive momentum (Stochastic cross-up, Supertrend bullish) and fear sentiment (37/100) creates contrarian entry opportunity in oversold macro environment.
debate.key_bear_argument: Weak ADX (10.87) negates trend confirmation, overbought Stochastic (84.5) and StochRSI limit upside, zero fundamental conviction (no insider buying, earnings risk in 28 days), and severe macro headwinds (VIX crisis, rising dollar, recession yield curve) make risk/reward unfavorable.

decision.entry_rationale: Technical structure is bullish (price above MAs, Supertrend confirmation) and fear sentiment presents contrarian opportunity, but weak trend confirmation (ADX 10.87) and overbought conditions severely limit upside potential.
decision.primary_risk: Severe macro headwinds (VIX crisis, rising dollar, recession yield curve) combined with earnings event in 28 days and zero fundamental conviction create asymmetric downside risk with limited upside.
decision.agent_agreement: strong — all agents aligned on bear case
decision.portfolio_note: Already holding SNPS with 38 existing IT positions (8.6% of portfolio); concentration risk and sector saturation argue against adding exposure.
